name: Diagonal Difference
description: Given a square matrix, calculate the absolute difference between the sum of its primary diagonal (top-left to bottom-right) and the sum of its secondary diagonal (top-right to bottom-left).
shortDescription: Absolute difference between the two diagonal sums

methods.label: Single pass

explanation.idea: The primary diagonal is where row equals column (i, i). The secondary diagonal is where row + column = n − 1 (i, n − 1 − i). One loop over i reaches both.
explanation.analogy: Two strings stretched across a square board corner to corner: you only need to step along each string, not look at every square.

computeWithSinglePass.summary: Add matrix[i][i] and matrix[i][n − 1 − i] for each row.
steps: For each row i, add matrix[i][i] to primary.
computeWithSinglePass.timeWhy: n steps for an n × n matrix.

computeWithFullScan.summary: Visit every cell and test whether it's on either diagonal.
steps: For every (i, j): if i == j add it; if i + j == n − 1 subtract it.
A centre cell on both diagonals is added and subtracted, which is correct.

pitfalls: Off by one on the secondary diagonal: it's n − 1 − i, not n − i.
interview: A HackerRank-style warm-up: point out that the single pass touches only 2n cells instead of n².
